exercise1.prompt: Formatting Numbers: The middle, with its ends

hiddenCases.name: a single value is its own mean and both ends
the mean is computed, not copied from an end
the summary is computed, not typed
hiddenCases.describe: the smallest and largest values alongside the mean

exercise1.hint: Compute all three, round each to one place with float() so they print as plain numbers, and build the sentence with an f-string.

exercise2.prompt: Formatting Numbers: Round once, at the end

hiddenCases.name: rounding the inputs first would give a different answer
more places keep more of the answer
zero places gives a whole number
a single value rounds to itself

exercise2.hint: Take s.mean() at full precision, then round once. Calling s.round(places) first would round every value before averaging, which is a different calculation.

choices: At the end, for display only
questions.explain: Rounding early puts the error into every calculation that follows.

questions.prompt: Reporting a mean as 72.4183 from nine observations does what?
choices: Claims precision the data does not support
questions.explain: The extra digits are noise dressed as certainty.
The percent format multiplies by 100 and appends the sign, formatting without changing the stored value.

questions.prompt: Why report min and max beside a mean?
choices: Two very different columns can share a mean
questions.explain: 70/71/72 and 10/71/132 both average 71, and only one supports "they scored about 71".
